title: Things to Do in Ziro: Apatani Villages, Rice-Fish Fields & the Music Festival
seoTitle: Things to Do in Ziro Valley: Villages & Festival | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Ziro Valley: walk the Apatani villages of Hong, Hari and Hija, see rice-fish paddy fields, visit Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary, hike to Kile Pakho, see the Siddheshwar Nath temple, attend the Ziro Music Festival, Myoko and Dree festivals.
dek: A high, flat valley ringed by pine-clad hills, where the Apatani people have farmed rice and fish together for generations and an independent music festival takes over every September.
searchIntent: Travellers planning three to four days in Ziro, often timed for the Ziro Music Festival, and wanting to understand Apatani culture respectfully.

hero.caption: Paddy fields, Ziro

intro: Ziro Valley, at about 1,500 metres in Lower Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh, is home to the Apatani people. Their system of wet rice cultivation, in which fish are raised in the same flooded fields, and their managed bamboo and pine groves have been studied as a model of sustainable land use, and the landscape is on India's tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage status.

The things to do in Ziro are about walking through villages and fields, learning about Apatani culture, and enjoying the valley's cool climate. Many people come in late September for the Ziro Music Festival, an independent music festival in the fields.
Plan three to four days, given the long journey in. An Inner Line Permit is required for Indian nationals.
quickAnswer: Walk through Hong, one of the largest Apatani villages
See the Myoko or Dree festival
Try Apatani food and rice beer

items.name: Walk through Hong

image.alt: Traditional Apatani bamboo house in Ziro
image.caption: Apatani house

body: Hong is one of the largest Apatani villages, with rows of bamboo-and-wood houses on stilts, ceremonial poles (babo) and platforms (lapang) where village councils meet. A local guide can explain clan structure, beliefs and customs.
Some older Apatani women have facial tattoos and nose plugs, a practice discontinued decades ago. Treat people with respect: ask before photographing anyone, and do not treat people as a spectacle.

items.name: See the rice-fish fields

image.alt: Apatani rice paddies in Ziro Valley
image.caption: Rice-fish paddies

body: Apatani fields are irrigated through a network of channels, and fish are raised in the paddy water, feeding on insects and fertilising the soil. Millet is grown on the bunds. Walking along the field paths shows how carefully the system is managed.

facts.Best time: June to September for green fields; September to October for harvest

items.name: Visit Hari and Hija
body: Hari and Hija are other Apatani villages with similar architecture and fields, and are often quieter than Hong. Homestays in these villages offer home-cooked meals and conversations about Apatani life.

items.name: Visit Talley Valley
body: Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary, about 30 km from Ziro, protects subtropical and temperate forest with rich birdlife and wildlife, including the clouded leopard. Permits are needed from the forest department, and the road is rough.

items.name: Hike to Kile Pakho
body: Kile Pakho is a ridge above the valley with views of Ziro on one side and the hills on the other. It makes a pleasant half-day hike through pine forest.

items.name: See the Siddheshwar Nath temple
body: The Siddheshwar Nath temple, in the Kardo forest, houses a large natural lingam discovered in 2004. It draws pilgrims especially at Mahashivratri.

items.name: Walk through the pine and bamboo groves
body: The Apatani manage pine and bamboo groves around the villages for timber and building material. Walks through them are cool and quiet, with birdsong.

items.name: Cycle or walk between villages
body: Ziro's valley floor is fairly flat, and the roads and paths between Hong, Hari, Hija, Bamin and Michi Bamin are pleasant to walk or cycle. Some homestays can arrange bicycles and local guides.

items.name: Attend the Ziro Music Festival

image.alt: Day stage at the Ziro Music Festival
image.caption: Ziro Music Festival

body: Held in late September, the Ziro Music Festival brings independent bands from India and abroad to an open-air stage in the fields. Campsites and homestays fill up fast; book early, and bring rain gear.

items.name: See Myoko and Dree
body: Myoko, in March, is the main Apatani festival of friendship and prosperity, with rituals by village priests. Dree, in July, is an agricultural festival with prayers for a good harvest.

items.name: Try Apatani food
body: Local food includes smoked meats, bamboo shoot dishes, sticky rice and apong (rice beer). Homestays are the best place to try it.

items.name: Spring (March to May)
body: Green fields, Myoko celebrations in March and mild weather. A good time for quieter visits.

items.name: Monsoon and harvest (June to October)
body: The fields are lush in the monsoon, though rain can disrupt roads. By September and October, the rice turns golden and the Music Festival takes place.

items.name: Winter (November to February)
body: Cold, clear days and frosty mornings. Fields are bare after the harvest, but skies are clear and the valley is very quiet.

byTraveller.text: Plan around the Ziro Music Festival and add a day or two to explore villages.
Stay in a village homestay, walk with a local guide and visit during Myoko.
Talley Valley and the ridge walks.

oneDay: Walk through Hong village with a local guide in the morning, then along the paddy fields to Hari. After lunch in a homestay, visit the Siddheshwar Nath temple and hike to a viewpoint for sunset.
tips: Apply for the Arunachal ILP online before you travel.
The nearest railway station is Naharlagun, about four hours away; Ziro has a small airport with limited flights.
Nights are cool; carry a jacket even in summer.
Respect village customs: ask before entering homes or photographing rituals, and follow your guide's advice at sacred sites.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Ziro?
faqs.a: Walk through Apatani villages such as Hong, Hari and Hija, see rice-fish fields, visit Talley Valley and Kile Pakho, see the Siddheshwar Nath temple and attend the Ziro Music Festival.

faqs.q: When is the Ziro Music Festival?
Do I need a permit for Ziro?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian nationals need an Inner Line Permit; foreign nationals need a Protected Area Permit.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for Ziro?
faqs.a: Three to four days, given the long journey.
The nearest railway station is Naharlagun, near Itanagar, about four hours by road. Ziro has a small airport with limited flights, and Guwahati is a long day's drive away.
